pages.text:
Vilmorin-Andrieux et Cie, "Les plantes potagères: description et culture des
principaux légumes des climats tempérés". Paris, 1891 (second edition).

Gallica / Bibliothèque nationale de France, ark:/12148/bpt6k8630130c
BnF, département Sciences et techniques, shelfmark 8-S-6938
Chapter TOMATE, printed pp. ~632-644 (document pages f0656-f0672).

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
--------------------
The work was acquired on 2026-08-30 as 18 page images plus 14 variety woodcuts
and a SOURCE.txt. It therefore had NO text document, and so NO row in the
catalogue at all: build_index.py excludes SOURCE.txt by name as bookkeeping, and
demotes an image with five or more siblings to a page of a set rather than a
work. The acquisition's provenance row consequently matched nothing, which is how
the gap was found -- import_provenance.py reported
"1 rows matched no document: 1891.les_plantes_potageres.vilmorin_andrieux".

The passages below were transcribed by the 2026-08-30 acquisition session and
were recorded only in SOURCE.txt. That breaks the standing rule that SOURCE.txt
must never hold the only copy of evidence, because it is deliberately not a
catalogue document. THIS FILE MOVES THAT EVIDENCE WHERE THE CATALOGUE CAN READ
IT. Nothing here is new: it is the earlier session's transcription, reproduced
verbatim, not a fresh reading of the page images.

THIS IS A PARTIAL TRANSCRIPTION -- THREE PASSAGES, NOT THE CHAPTER
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Only the three passages the earlier session quoted are below. The remaining
pages of the TOMATE chapter are HELD AS IMAGES BUT NOT TRANSCRIBED. A term search
over this file is therefore a search of three quotations, not of the chapter: a
zero here is not evidence that a word is absent from Vilmorin 1891. The page
images in tomate_chapter_pages/ are the actual evidence and are what should be
read.

TRANSCRIBED PASSAGES
====================

[printed p. 633] TOMATE ROUGE GROSSE

très gros, déprimés, irrégulièrement côtelés, larges de 0m,07 à 0m,10,
épais de 0m,04 à 0m,05

-- and, on the same page, the observation that tomato canning is
"une industrie très développée" in the Midi.

[printed p. 636] TOMATE ROUGE GROSSE LISSE (English: "Trophy tomato")

difficile à conserver absolument pure; les fruits tendent toujours à
redevenir côtelés.

[printed p. 636] TOMATE CHAMPION

très lisses, bien faits et passablement déprimés

rouge violacé et non franchement écarlate

WHAT THESE PASSAGES CARRY
-------------------------
Scored fruit morphology in the grower's own words, with measurements:

ROUGE GROSSE shape flat/depressed (déprimés)
ribbing STRONG and irregular (irrégulièrement côtelés)
size 70-100 mm wide x 40-50 mm thick
ROUGE GROSSE LISSE a SMOOTH selection that reverts -- "les fruits tendent
toujours à redevenir côtelés" is a direct statement that
smoothness is the unstable state and ribbing the one the
population returns to. That is the single most useful
sentence in the acquisition.
CHAMPION smooth, well formed, fairly depressed; colour
"rouge violacé", explicitly NOT frank scarlet.

The variety woodcuts in 1891.les_plantes_potageres.vilmorin/ are captioned
"Fruits de grosseur naturelle" -- life size -- so they are scale-bearing and can
be measured directly against the printed page.

NOT TRANSCRIBED, AND WORTH DOING
--------------------------------
Gallica's ContentSearch located "tomate" on document pages 12, 31, 112, 500,
680, 724, 736, 742, 745, 752, 754 and 755. Only f0012 and the chapter itself
(f0656-f0672) were fetched; the rest of the 764-page volume is not held. See
SOURCE.txt for how to complete it.
